issues.title: Recovery notes template is singular but multi-agent stall is a known scenario
issues.details: The plan's Problem section describes recovering two stalled agents in one run (researcher + checker). The Recovery notes template in offer_next, auto-advance, and step 0a all use singular phrasing ('the stalled agent name', 'agent name, accepted/repaired artifact'). An operator recovering two agents would need to improvise the format.
issues.suggested_fix: Pluralize the template hint: 'Recovery notes: {None | For each recovered agent: agent name, artifact accepted/repaired, validation performed, inline fallback used yes/no}' — or add a brief note that recovery notes repeat per recovered agent.

issues.title: Implementation scope is broader than plan's deviation-note requirement
issues.details: The plan says 'Require an explicit deviation note...whenever recovery uses inline completion or accepts disk artifacts without a marker.' The implementation in step 0a says 'Any use of this recovery path must be surfaced' — which includes scenarios where the marker was found in a stable disk artifact (no inline, no missing marker). This is a safe widening, not a contradiction.
issues.suggested_fix: No fix needed. The broader requirement is strictly safer. Optionally update the plan's Proposed Patch bullet to match ('whenever the recovery path is used' instead of the narrower condition).

review.best_case: The patch plan and implementation are aligned and ready to ship. All three focus items are verified present. The recovery contract is generic enough to cover all seven spawn sites while providing concrete scenario guidance for the three most likely stall types. The 0a/9a/11a disambiguation prevents operators from confusing live-stalled agents with returned-without-marker agents.
strongest_objections: The Recovery notes template uses singular phrasing despite the motivating incident involving two stalled agents — an operator hitting the same scenario would have to improvise multi-entry formatting
The plan doc's Proposed Patch bullet describes a narrower deviation-note trigger than what the implementation actually enforces, creating minor drift between plan and implementation
Pattern mapper and chunked-planner stall scenarios rely entirely on the generic contract without dedicated walkthroughs, though this was an accepted peer-review decision
hidden_assumptions: The 10-minute default wait budget is assumed reasonable for all agent types and all model speeds — a very fast model or a very slow research task could make this threshold wrong

The stable-size/mtime check (two checks 10 seconds apart) assumes the filesystem clock resolution is fine enough to detect changes — network-mounted filesystems with coarse timestamps could miss writes
The inline fallback bounds assume the orchestrator can reliably scope itself to 'current artifact only' without accidentally broadening phase scope in practice
review.what_would_change_my_mind: If an actual multi-agent stall recovery attempt showed that the singular Recovery notes template caused the operator to drop one agent's recovery from the closeout, that would upgrade the WARN to a blocker. If the 10-minute wait budget proved systematically wrong for a common model/task combination, the trigger definition would need parameterization beyond 'unless the local runtime has a stricter configured wait budget.'
